result.title: DecoyCount: Evaluating Visual-Reasoning Misalignment in Counting
result.summary: Visual counting benchmarks report whether vision-language models produce the correct number, but not whether errors arise from perception or reasoning. We introduce DecoyCount, a benchmark built from 1,660 real-world images with designed decoys across seven mechanisms, along with paired prompts: a neutral question, a matched alignment cue, and a novel multi-hop, multi-image question that situates the same counting problem in a realistic scenario. Using this design, we find that counting failures are induced partly by visual misalignment: models can execute the intended counting process when cue-guided but fail to select it unaided, and we term this difference in accuracy the reasoning-alignment gap. Despite being highly capable on general reasoning, frontier models remain below 50\% accuracy on our benchmark, while alignment gaps range from 11.8-22.1 percentage points; strikingly, we observe that more capable models, greater thinking budgets, and agentic processes often induce larger gaps. Because humans may bring context that models lack, we test whether textual underspecification contributes to misalignment using a scenario-based multi-hop condition without explicit hinting, but this added context does not improve aggregate performance. Our analysis concludes that stronger general reasoning does not by itself generalize to aligned visual reasoning, leaving misalignment with human visual expectations as a substantial component of the remaining deficit.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DecoyCount 计数基准：基于 1,660 张真实图像，设计七类干扰机制，并配套中性提问、对齐线索提问与多跳多图提问三种提示，以区分计数错误源自感知还是推理，并将提示前后的准确率差定义为 reasoning-alignment gap。
AI.relevance_reason: 该诊断直接检验模型能否自发选取与视觉证据对齐的推理路径，而非仅执行被指明的过程；其「thinking budget 与 agentic 流程越大、对齐差距越大」的发现，可供核查 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的收益边界及视觉证据筛选机制。
